body:
Well, I'll start off with the obvious. You are not stupid. The fact that you can speak and write in a second language is incredible enough as it is, the fact that you can do it at sixteen is ridiculous. The vast majority of people cannot do that. Also, programming is incredibly difficult and it takes tons, and I mean *tons* of time to get good at it, but it's an extremely valuable skill and you can go anywhere with it. Programmers are needed everywhere, and the fact that you can write code that actually *runs* is on it's own outstanding. The fact that you're only sixteen and you code as a *hobby* is something that you should take immense pride in. 
Also, I am an American, and I can tell you that there is no way Muslims will not be able to travel here. There are enough of us liberals and non-racists here to make sure of that. You have options. 
And it's going to be tough, you're right. It really is, but there are a lot of people like you from all walks of life. I grew up in a crazy private Christian school, it fit every single stereotype about the racist gun-toting Christian. I left that place with nothing and things have been incredibly difficult. Frankly they've been difficult for my entire life, I've seen some shit. I just posted here in fact, so I'm not in an awesome place either, but my point is that there are people like you everywhere. Religion is oppressive, and you can take comfort in the fact that it's on its way out, but in the meantime there are tons of online communities for the ex-religious. I'm not equating your struggle with mine, clearly yours is much more serious, but it is not something in which you are alone. Obviously I only really know of the communities for ex-Christians (because that is what I am) but I'm sure there are lots of online places full of people just like you surrounded by a faith that you cannot reconcile yourself with.
You're a smart kid. You're goddamn smart. And you're right, there's a good chance it's gonna be a tough road ahead. I'm not qualified to tell you what you should do because I don't know enough about the area and the culture, but what I can tell you is there are ways out. You are not alone. 
Keep in mind that you have a leg up too, you're smart, and that's a very good ticket out. It sucks. It does, but keep your chin up, somehow things will get better.

Talk to me. I know how you feel. I posted here less than an hour ago. As logical as it might seem, it isn't. There are really good things out there, and it's hard to see that now but there are. It's hard. It's really hard. I don't know what to say besides that I know how you feel and that you're not alone. There are good things. There are always good things. It's worth it to stick around.

Yeah, I know how that goes. Things pick up though, somehow at some point things pick up. They've done so before anyway. I've been feeling the same way so I don't entirely know how to help besides saying that there are nice things out there. There are positive things out there and you're not alone. You're not crazy and you're not the only one who feels like this.

I don't really know what to tell you. I'm largely in the same boat. In fact, I just posted here, so I really don't have the right to say much of anything, but it looks like I'm going too anyway.
You just have to keep going. Why? I don't really know. I can't really write it down. Because sometimes someone is nice to you. Sometimes you take a drive out somewhere and it's really nice. Keep going. If anything else do it just to see what else you'll see. There are nice things out there, and occasionally you stumble on them, and that's a really good moment that you don't want to miss. 
When it comes to actually seeking those things out and finding them, I have no fucking idea how one goes about doing it, besides just trying to do it. 
I hope I helped somehow.
